disease_details.symptoms: Water-soaked polygonal angular spots on leaves turning purplish-brown, centers drop out giving a 'shot-hole' look. Pitted, gumming lesions on fruit.
disease_details.spread_mechanism: Bacteria splash from twig cankers during wind-driven rain and enter via stomata and wounds.
prevention_steps: Plant resistant peach cultivars (e.g., Candor, Clayton, Reliance).
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilizers that stimulate susceptible young shoot growth.
Plant windbreaks to reduce windblown sand abrasions that facilitate bacterial entry.
organic_controls: Dormant copper applications and low-rate copper hydroxide during early cover sprays.
chemical_controls: Bactericides: Oxytetracycline (Mycoshield) and low-rate copper formulations applied from petal fall through cover sprays.
disease_details.when_to_consult_expert: If twig cankers proliferate or fruit drop exceeds 10%.
safety_notes: Always read and strictly follow pesticide product label instructions and pre-harvest intervals (PHI).
Wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including chemical-resistant gloves, goggles, and respirator mask.
Keep all chemicals out of reach of children and away from livestock and drinking water sources.
Consult your local agricultural extension officer or call Kisan Call Center (1800-180-1551) for certified advice.

What is this?
Apple Scab
Possible Apple Scab. Compare the symptoms before choosing treatment.
Olive-green to dark brown velvety spots on leaves, becoming corky and distorted. Scabby lesions on fruit surface leading to cracking.
What to do now
Apply sulfur or liquid lime-sulfur sprays preventatively prior to rain events during primary infection season.
Apply Bacillus subtilis or potassium bicarbonate sprays.
Organic options
Apply sulfur or liquid lime-sulfur sprays preventatively prior to rain events during primary infection season.
Apply Bacillus subtilis or potassium bicarbonate sprays.
Chemical options
Read the label first

Read the product label. Wear the required protective clothing, gloves and mask. Keep pesticides away from children and water sources. Confirm the product, dose and waiting period with your local agriculture office.

Always read and strictly follow pesticide product label instructions and pre-harvest intervals (PHI).
Wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including chemical-resistant gloves, goggles, and respirator mask.
Keep all chemicals out of reach of children and away from livestock and drinking water sources.

Preventative protectants: Captan, Mancozeb (FRAC M04, M03).
Systemic fungicides: DMI fungicides (FRAC 3, e.g., Myclobutanil) or SDHI fungicides (FRAC 7, e.g., Fluopyram) in rotation to avoid resistance.
Prevention
Rake and destroy fallen leaves in autumn or shred with a flail mower to speed decomposition.
Prune tree canopies to improve airflow and sunlight penetration.
Plant scab-resistant cultivars (e.g., Enterprise, GoldRush, Liberty, Prima).
Ask an expert
If leaf lesions cover more than 20% of the canopy before petal fall or if commercial fruit quality is at risk.

Gymnosporangium juniperi-virginianae

What is this?
Cedar Apple Rust
Possible Cedar Apple Rust. Compare the symptoms before choosing treatment.
Bright yellow-orange circular spots on upper leaf surfaces. Raised tubular structures (aecia) on leaf undersides and fruit.
What to do now
Liquid sulfur or sulfur-based sprays applied preventatively when cedar galls swell in spring.
Organic options
Liquid sulfur or sulfur-based sprays applied preventatively when cedar galls swell in spring.
Chemical options
Read the label first

Read the product label. Wear the required protective clothing, gloves and mask. Keep pesticides away from children and water sources. Confirm the product, dose and waiting period with your local agriculture office.

Always read and strictly follow pesticide product label instructions and pre-harvest intervals (PHI).
Wear required Personal Protective Equipment (PPE) including chemical-resistant gloves, goggles, and respirator mask.
Keep all chemicals out of reach of children and away from livestock and drinking water sources.
Consult your local agricultural extension officer or call Kisan Call Center (1800-180-1551) for certified advice.
Sterol inhibitor / DMI fungicides (FRAC 3, e.g., Myclobutanil, Tebuconazole) or Strobilurins (FRAC 11) from pink bud through third cover.
Prevention
Remove nearby Eastern red cedar / juniper trees within a 1-2 mile radius where feasible.
Remove rust galls (cedar apples) from adjacent landscape junipers before spring rains.
Plant rust-resistant apple varieties (e.g., Liberty, Freedom, Enterprise).
Ask an expert
If premature defoliation exceeds 30% of tree canopy in consecutive seasons.

University of Missouri Extension: Cedar Apple Rust (G6026)
